design_intent.original_text: Make it a 3x3x3 cube with no gravity: players still alternate placing X and O in any empty cell; any straight line of three cells through the cube (rows, columns, pillars and every diagonal, 49 lines in total) wins; a full cube with no line is a draw.
preserve: Players alternate turns placing X and O.
changes: Remove gravity; a player may place their mark in any empty cell.
Award a win for any straight line of three cells through the cube, including rows, columns, pillars, and every diagonal: 49 winning lines in total.
Declare a draw when the cube is full and neither player has a winning line.
constraints: Marks may be placed only in empty cells.
unresolved: Conversation and turn identifiers were not provided.

lift_plan.source_xy_policy: Keep the bounded x and y axes at extent 3, their coordinates, empty/X/O cell values, X-first alternating turns, and the existing placement, restart, and quit behavior. Add no gravity.
lift_plan.neighborhood: Winning lines use straight, contiguous triples along the three axes and all face and body diagonals: 27 axial lines, 18 face diagonals, and 4 body diagonals, for 49 lines total.
lift_plan.movement: On a turn, place the current player's mark in any empty (x,y,z) cell. Reject occupied or out-of-bounds targets without changing state. Do not allow placements after a win or draw. Restart resets all 27 cells and the turn; quit retains its Source behavior.
lift_plan.outcomes: After each legal placement, a line of three matching marks anywhere in the cube wins for its owner. Check wins before declaring a draw; a draw requires every cube cell occupied and no winning line.
lift_plan.presentation: Show the board as one continuous cube volume using the engine-owned cell shells, 3D positions, colliders, and overview camera. Display X and O in their occupied cells and retain turn, winner, and draw status.
lift_plan.input: Click a cube cell to supply its full (x,y,z) coordinate. Use the engine-provided '[' and ']' keys or on-screen buttons to select a depth layer when picking inner cells. Retain R to restart and Escape to quit.
z_equals_one_tests: With z at extent 1, legal placements and occupied-cell rejection must match the Source 3×3 board.
With z at extent 1, exactly the Source rows, columns, and two diagonals win; a full board without a line draws.
With z at extent 1, X moves first, turns alternate, and restart restores the Source initial state.

source_game_spec.summary: Two players alternate placing X and O on a 3×3 grid; three in a row wins, and a full board without a win is a draw.

initial_setup.description: Every cell is empty; X moves first, with no winner or draw.

actions.legal_when: There is no winner or draw, x and y are each within 0 through 2, and board[y][x] is empty.
actions.effect: Set board[y][x] to the current player's value. Check for a win, then a draw; only if neither occurs, switch the current player from 1 to 2 or from 2 to 1. An illegal placement returns false without changing state.

actions.legal_when: An R keydown is received; the source imposes no game-state restriction.
actions.effect: Reset the board, current player, winner, and draw state to their initial values.

actions.legal_when: Escape is pressed or a window-close event is received.
actions.effect: Stop the application loop; no game outcome is assigned.

outcomes.condition: After a placement, any row, column, or either diagonal has all three cells equal to the current player's value.
After a placement, no winning line exists and every board cell is nonzero.

controls.control: Left-button down; convert pointer position to a cell using the board's left and top offsets and cell size.

presentation.description: A Pygame window displays a status line showing the turn, winner, or draw; instructions; and a 3×3 board of rounded cells with blue X marks and orange O marks. The display loop is capped at 60 frames per second.
